And in that document we are going to look at the first bullet point referring to the enemy where it says, and I quote the second paragraph of this document, reads: "We believe that in the forthcoming period, the enemy will intensify offensive activities against the Drina Corps area of responsibility, mainly in the Tuzla, Zvornik, and Kladanj Vlasenica directions with simultaneous activity by the 28th Division forces from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa in order to cut the Drina Corps area of responsibility in two and connect the enclaves with the central part of the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina which is held by the Muslim forces." Please, bearing all this in mind, my question is as follows: Did they manage to pull out from the enclaves? I'm referring to the Muslim troops in Zepa and Srebrenica. And did they manage to link up with the forces in Kladanj and Tuzla? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that some of the troops, some of the elements of the army managed to link up with them. Some troops were disarmed and, according to the information that was available to us and the general public in Bosnia-Herzegovina as well as the international general public, some of the elements went in the direction of Serbia. They crossed the Drina River and ended up on the other side. Two days ago I mentioned that the elements, or smaller groups, continued to look for ways to link up with their forces for a number of days thereafter and there were still losses at this time when I was hospitalised, after having been wounded, and the officers from the command of my brigade visited me and informed me about the losses that happened even after both tasks had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could it be said that the Muslims did not manage to link up the territories of the enclaves with Tuzla, however, they managed to pull out some of their soldiers, as you have said, and some of their ammunition, and link up with the majority of forces in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the objective of their activities, as it says here in the document, for the enclaves to be linked up, which they didn't manage to do because one of the enclaves fell, and automatically that changed the status of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You as brigade commander, did you receive information prior to that that starting from the spring of 1995, Muslims had been conducting active combat operations towards the territory of Republika Srpska, precisely in order to conquer territory, link up their territories, break up Republika Srpska and its army?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such information came in via official correspondence, it was sent to subordinate units, and it was reported in the media as well, about sabotage activities in the area, in the villages surrounding the enclaves, where there were various misdeeds - that's exactly the right word, misdeeds - and atrocities committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we will look at D52 in e-court. This is the document of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina dated the 8th of July 1995, where they provide information about the combat results of their units and the soldiers of the 28th Division. We don't need to read the entire document because it's known to all of the parties, but please look at the first bullet point, where he informs his own 2nd Corps by saying 60 Chetniks were liquidated and, according to unconfirmed reports, the aggressor suffered even greater losses and had many wounded. Then in the second bullet point he says that 16 automatic rifles, three machine-guns, and so on and so on, were captured. I would like to ask you this: Does this indicate that there were active combat operations conducted by the troops of the 28th Division from the territory of the Srebrenica safe haven towards the area where your troops were; and as a result, did they kill the number of civilians indicated here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is yet another indicator of the fact that there were active combat operations, and we see here the analysis of these operations. And it's written here, in order to strengthen the combat morale of their troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps General Tolimir misspoke but I don't think there is any reference in this section that he's citing to civilians, and in fact, I think General Tolimir himself has acknowledged on a prior occasion that this was a military target and these were military losses, I think as evidenced by the amount of military hardware. As I said, maybe he misspoke when he referred to them as civilians, but I think it's worth clarifying, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir asked, "... did they kill the number of civilians indicated here?" We see in the document 60 Chetniks were liquidated. I would like to ask the witness: Do you know anything about the question if they were civilians, these 60 people, or military personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is how I would interpret this: In the first bullet point, it says 60 Chetniks were liquidated. And we also used derogatory terms. We called the opposing side Turks and they called us Chetniks. We all used derogatory terms, so let me interpret this in my way. 60 Chetniks were liquidated, and then they go on to list various things, and they say, according to unconfirmed reports, the aggressor suffered even greater losses, and so on. So the 60 people were killed and the number of the wounded is not known because everybody was pulled out. And if we add up the weapons that were captured, we can see that there were 16 plus 3 plus 1 plus 1 carbine, so there was a total of 21 pieces of weapons. That is to say 21 soldiers. And the remaining were Chetniks, if I can use their term, Chetniks without weapons. They go on to say that there were livestock seized, and this indicates that all this transpired in a village. And they also mention a van. They don't mention a military vehicle, they mention a van. So according to their report, I would say that there was, at the most, a platoon here of up to 25 men, and then the remaining persons were civilians, between 25 and 60, the remaining persons were civilians, because we can see that they also captured livestock in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me clarify the following: Is that a conclusion you have drawn from this document or is it your personal knowledge at that time when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is my conclusion after reading this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you hear that the village of Visnjica, which was not at the front line, was attacked and that there were victims there? Or were other villages around Srebrenica attacked, villages that were not in the theatre of war or at the front line? Were other villages in the territory of Republika Srpska attacked?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard of such operations, and I know of losses that were incurred further in the depth of the territory, not just at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please explain to us, what do you mean, not just at the front line? What is the distance between the demarcation line and the depth of the territory where there were losses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the rules, the front area covers some 100 to 150 metres, and this is where the platoons are deployed, and that further into the depth is the area normally held by a battalion, which has the depth of 3 kilometres, typically. So after this front area, which covers 100 to 150 metres, further in the depth losses were incurred in the areas held by battalions; that is to say 3 kilometres further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see 153, please. While we are waiting for the document, let me say that this looks to be a document of the General Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you tell us, 153 is not a document. Are you referring to P153 or D153?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I wrote down incorrectly. It should be D53, D53. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this be zoomed in, please, so that the witness can see it. Otherwise the font is too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a document of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina which is a -- which is dated 17th of June - that is to say, a month before the attack on the enclave - where it says, "Preparations for offensive of combat operations, order." Before we start dealing with the document, can you tell the Chamber what offensive combat operations are. What does that term encompass? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it? I wasn't focused on your question, I was reading the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, describe as a soldier, what "combat offensive operations" are, or "offensive combat operations" are.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Offensive combat operations are all operations which include activities, or, rather, which, based on the initiative in the combat, offensive combat operations are various incursions, attacks; everything that means having the initiative in relation to the opposing side. In other words, active combat operations, with the objective of moving in to attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see here an order issued by Rasim Delic, the commander of the 2nd Corps, Brigadier Sulejman Budakovic sent to the 28th Division. That is to say that this order came from the corps command in Tuzla and it was sent to the 28th Division. It says here: "Pursuant to a verbal order of the commander of the General Staff of the BH Army, army General Rasim Delic, and on the occasion of the great success achieved by units of the BH Army in the wide area around Sarajevo and Gorazde, and also on the basis of intelligence that the AS command of the Protection Regiment in Han Pijesak is holding part of its units in reserve to intervene in the event of an attack by our forces from Zepa, I hereby order." And then under number 1: "Execute all preparations in the command of the 28th Land Army Division to execute offensive combat operations with a view to liberate the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina overstretching the aggressor forces and inflicting losses on them, coordinating action with the BH Army forces carrying out operations in the broader Sarajevo area." Now, based on what I have just read, my question to you is: One month before the Muslim forces left the enclave of Srebrenica, does the corps commander from Tuzla order his forces that offensive combat operations be carried out from this protected area? And if so, could you explain which offensive combat operations these were? And did this happen one month before the Army of Republika Srpska prevented such activities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. Quite clearly, this is an order to conduct preparations for combat operations, and its objective clearly is once the task is issued to commence with offensive activities, to act in concert with the forces carrying out operations in the Sarajevo area. This is quite a logical military procedure, and it is clear here that further activities are continued, further activities of various kinds, in order to enable larger operations in some other area for which tasks are not yet issued, but the General Staff will issue its order to regulate that. Something along the lines of the task given by the Drina Corps concerning the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could we see D67 in e-court, please. Again, this is a document of the BH Army signed by Rasim Delic, and this document was sent via the 1st Corps by [as interpreted] the president of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm interested in the fourth bullet point. Would you please look at it and I will read it. It's on page 2 in the English. It says here: "In preparation for a future operation to link up the enclaves, we brought in and took back four brigade commanders, two brigade chiefs of staff, and the Chief of Staff of the 26th Division. The Division commander, who was meant to go on the next helicopter flight, did not return. After the final flight ended tragically, Naser remained." What I want to ask you is this: Based on this, can it be seen that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina prepared even before, even prior to that time, the linking up of the enclaves protected by the 28th Division in Zepa, and was it their goal to link up that area with the territory under the control of the 2nd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is obvious. This is a very clear document dated the 13th of July, as I can see. It was sent at 1500 hours. Preparations were underway, irrespective of the fact that the enclave of Srebrenica had fallen, as it were. It is obvious that some of the elements had pulled out and linked up with the main body of the troops. Plans were being made for future operations with a view to linking up the forces from the enclaves with the main body of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I would like to refer to page 53, line 8. You are recorded to having said, "This document was sent via the 1st Corps by the president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina." I think this document is sent to the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for having asked me to remove this mistake from the transcript, which is exactly what I am doing now. General Delic sent this report to Alija Izetbegovic via the commander of the 1st Corps after the fall of enclave to demonstrate what they had been up to before the fall of the enclave and this is what I meant, this is what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just wanted to clarify, "by the president" is wrong; it should be "to the president." Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, I apologise to you as well. I didn't tell you and I didn't allow you to read the entire document. Let me tell you that this document was drafted after the fall of the enclave. It was written by Rasim Delic, it was sent to the president of the Presidency in order to tell him what had been undertaken before the fall of the enclave. In this document, he says that whatever I have read out to you, that preparations were underway for future operations and that the brigade commanders had been returned. This is something that is a fait accompli, something they had done already. I'm asking you now, because of these activities and similar activities that they undertook, is that why Krivaja operation was launched? Does this document show that they were engaged in certain military activities in order to prepare what the reports sent to Alija Izetbegovic describes? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document clarifies the situation somewhat. And you're absolutely right. Based on this report, you can tell that preparations were underway in order to link up the enclaves. However, the attempt failed because the commander of the 28th Division did not manage to return to the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So you can see clearly that there were preparations going on for future operations. I'm repeating my question. In order to prevent those preparations from continuing, is that why operation Krivaja was launched, in order to disarm the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the operation was launched in order to narrow down the area, to prevent incursions, to narrow down the -- to reduce the enclaves which would prevent the linking up of the enclaves. They would be more apart and that was the goal, the main goal of Operation Krivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On the following pages of this document -- can they be shown to the witness -- you can see reference made to the quantities of weapons and ammunition which had been brought to Zepa and Srebrenica, which had been air lifted -- air dropped, and also reference is made to a helicopter that had been downed. Do you know anything about helicopter sorties from Tuzla bringing weapons for the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves and about accidents that those helicopters had?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I don't remember having heard any information about those sorties, and if I knew something, I've forgotten it in the meantime. I can't remember. There were talks about helicopter flights over Srebrenica and Tuzla but they didn't fly over my zone. And all of that was a regular occurrence, it was not something that I was concerned with at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your previous testimonies, for example, in the Popovic -- in the Popovic case, on page 11808, you described the preparations for Krivaja operation, and this is lines 19 through 13 [as interpreted], and you said: "I remember that everything was in keeping with the customary procedure. There was an intelligence service from the corps who briefed us about the situation and the estimates about the enemy forces. He also gave us an estimate about their strength and deployment according to what he knew, according to the intelligence that he was privy to. That was an officer that I had not seen before." And then in line 20 on the same page of the transcript, you said that that was Kosoric. Thank you. And based on what I have just read out, you will probably remember what you testified about. And my question is this: Did you learn from the intelligence officers of your command about the activities and attempts by the enemy before Operation Krivaja ever took place? If that was the case, can you just briefly tell us what they informed you about? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of our regular activities or as part of the intelligence officers' activities of my superior command, they sent us information and the reports arrived at the intelligence officers of the brigade and they informed us about the strength, the deployment, the intercepted conversations if there were any, the problems that could be noticed on the enemy side. So those reports contained all the intelligence that is normally gathered, and the reports were sent on a daily basis. As for your question about the intelligence officer being at the intelligence post at Pribicevac, he informed us about the task and he indicated the area where they were able to observe the firing point, the depth, the axis, the supply channels, and all that was in respect of the concrete task. All that was carried out at the Pribicevac observation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the Popovic case, transcript page 1180 -- 10, lines 8 through 14, you shared your understanding of the tasks and objectives of Krivaja operation, and I'm going to quote you - I don't want to rephrase your words - and I quote: "The main goal of the operation that was set out by the command -- I thank you, I apologise -- the main task -- the main goal of operation that was set out by the corps command as a result of the previous events and developments, the days and the months preceding that decision, was to break off the protective areas of Zepa and Srebrenica and to pull them apart from each other in view of the fact that there were constant incidents and sabotage actions being carried out from the protected area and that we suffered losses on the lines and in the villages in the immediate vicinity of the protected areas." And then on page 11884, you continued to say, in lines 12 through 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document P1197.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President, I apologise for not having said that before. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You continued to say: "We were given a task in respect of the elements of the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to engage them but to avoid any contact with members of the UNPROFOR and their check-points which were deployed along the length of the axis where our units were engaged in combat. We were also told that the objective of the operation was not the town of Srebrenica or its population." This is what you said in the Popovic transcript. Based on what I have just read out to you, my question is this: Could you please explain, when you say that the objective was not the population of the town of Srebrenica, what did you mean by that? What was supposed to be your conduct towards the civilian population and towards UNPROFOR? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my previous testimony and from the testimony in this case, there are some things that I would like to highlight: Not for a single moment, not in a single document, not in a single contact with my superiors did I ever hear any reference being made to opening fire on any indiscriminate target in order to enter Srebrenica. I have to go back to an interpretation and an analysis of one part of my testimony in the Blagojevic case, where I talked about the different stages that we went through. The developments and the goals were adapted to the situation on the ground. It was not at all cost that we planned from the outset to enter the settled area of Srebrenica. For example, my unit, and you can see that in my diary, my unit, on the 12th or, rather, already on the 10th of July, already had its march route changed and as the resistance subsided and as we say that we would be able not only to reduce the enclave of Srebrenica but come very close to it, that we should alter our original task and mission, and finally, our final goal became entering Srebrenica, which we did. Let me reiterate that there was no single order or single document that set out the tasks to be carried out at all cost, and that would be to enter Srebrenica irrespective of any losses that we might have suffered. The conduct towards UNPROFOR soldiers and their check-points was supposed to be correct, and that materialised at the moment when I came into contact with them. And as for the other people that I saw and that I came in contact with, and my conduct towards them was exactly as one might expect from civilised people and honest soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if you look at the clock, I think it's the proper time for our second break. The Chamber would appreciate if you could give us, after the break, an estimation of the length of your cross-examination. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. Your Honours, in response to your request about the time estimate we would need for cross-examination of this witness, we would like to tell you that we will require the entire day tomorrow, leaving some time for the

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: The other matter is that I would like to ask that P1231, which was marked for identification, be now admitted into evidence. That is the conversation between Colonel Trivic and one of the investigators, and this document was used in cross-examination just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was going to raise these problems as well. I wanted to know, if the cross-examination will not go over the full day tomorrow, if the Prosecution intends to call the witness Gallagher tomorrow, but I think now there is no need for a discussion about that. I'm referring to a motion we received, a confidential motion we received this morning. Perhaps I can ask the Defence if they had the chance to -- if they have already position to express or if they want to respond to that, if they are objecting or not. If that is possible. Otherwise, we should deal with that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, I have not seen any motions yet. I haven't opened my e-mail yet today. So we will reply to that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I can deal with that tomorrow at the beginning of our hearing. The other question I would like to mention is if we are sitting in the morning or in the afternoon tomorrow. We can't decide now. I think we have to wait -- we are scheduled for the afternoon. I know that many participants would prefer to sit in the morning. That depends on the progress another trial will make this afternoon. Therefore, I would like to remind everybody to be aware that we could reschedule the hearing from the afternoon to the morning for tomorrow. Please look at the -- your e-mails. Mr. Tolimir, please continue -- no, first, we receive as evidence P1231. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The witness spoke about the change of order given. Could we now see 65 ter 00197, which was tendered into evidence by the Prosecution. While we are waiting for it to come up on the screen, let me say that this is a document of the command of the Drina Corps, dated the 15th of May 1995. It is entitled, "Stabilisation of defence around the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves and creation of conditions for liberation of enclaves. Order." In the first item of this order, it says: "According to the information gathered, the Muslims are carrying out intensive preparations for offensive operations from the greater area of Tuzla, Kladanj, and Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, with the basic goal to cut the Republika Srpska territory, to connect the non-enclaves with the central part, the so-called Bosnia and Herzegovina, and access the Drina River. Simultaneous offensive activities are expected from the area of Kladanj and Kalesija. They will intensify infiltration of the reconnaissance and sabotage groups before the offensive operations on a larger scale, fully using the in-between areas and natural vegetation." So this is page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, this is P1217.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: We saw that this document is from May, Mr. Trivic. It was drafted in order to prevent the activities that I just read to you about. However, on the very next day -- this was written on the 15th of May, and then on the next day, this is the last page of 65 ter 00198 -- could we please see 00198. 65 ter 00198.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is P1218.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: So immediately on the following day, another document was drafted on the 16th of May. It was sent to all units, just like the first one, and in item 3 it says: "Forces at the western part of the front, Drina Corps area of responsibility and around Zepa enclave, will continue to defend firmly the positions taken." And in item 1, it says: "Due to insufficient number of troops for full implementation of the task of closing the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica, the order above is being amended and supplemented by the following." That means the one of the 15th of May. So in the first one, you were given an order to carry out certain operations, and in the second one they were withdrawing it due to insufficient number of troops. Would you please, as a soldier, explain what these two documents mean. Would you please explain it for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear that these two documents compose one order. I suppose that the assessment used for the first document was wrong, and when the subordinate units reacted to that document, then they gave up on the initial task and confirmed in writing that they were giving up on that task. However, the forces at the demarcation line were to continue trying to move the lines towards the enclaves, as far as possible, towards the enclave of Zepa, due to this constant contact between two enclaves. It is clear that these two documents should be read together as one document, and that the second one is a written correction indicating that the task issued in the first document was now changed.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Popovic case, at page 1193 of the transcript, when speaking of the offensive of the Muslims against Republika Srpska and the enclaves there, you said the following. I'm quoting: "There was an offensive conducted in various areas, including in the spring of 1995. The offensive was launched from the Tuzla area, I think towards the area held by the East Bosnia Corps and the Drina Corps. I was supposed to send some parts of my unit to provide assistance in the area of the Zvornik Brigade. If I remember well, I was supposed to do that because the brigade was being attacked in its own area of responsibility." Now, please tell me, given that you sent some of your forces to the Zvornik Brigade, which faced the Tuzla Corps of the BH Army, was there an intention by the Tuzla Corps and the BH Army to link up their forces from Tuzla with the forces which were in Srebrenica and Zepa? And what can you tell us about that in general?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a professional soldier, please allow me to answer that question. Each activity undertaken has a goal, in order to engage forces, men and resources, in order to provide support to them, in order to protect the people, this is not done randomly. There is always a goal when activities are being undertaken. And later on, if these goals are accomplished, then that improves the position of own forces. So I suppose that that was the goal of these activities, as far as can be seen from various documents of both armies, namely that each activity has a defined goal, a defined objective.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before this break, you spoke about the change in an order given, as we just saw, and you said that there were also changes made in the course of the combat, and allegedly you yourself did it on the 10th of July. Could we now see D431, please. We can see D431 here. This was sent by the Main Staff. I signed it. I apologise: D41. D41. This is an order signed by Krstic. This is the order we just saw, on the 16th of May, and now can we see, in e-court, D41? Thank you. Okay. We see it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I note for the record that this is not included in the list of documents to be used with this witness in cross-examination. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the same document can be found on the OTP list, but with a P number. So this is a known document. It is known both to us and the Prosecution, and I think that the document was used with this witness in another trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please give us the P number you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I would need to look it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's P690, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Could we now see in e-court D -- P690. We can see it in the English. Could we see it in the Serbian as well so that the witness can see what this was about and why the order was changed in the course of the combat in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: This is a document from the Main Staff, dated 9th of July, sent to the command of the Drina Corps, signed by Major General Zdravko Tolimir. It says: "The President of Republika Srpska --" I'm quoting now: "The President of Republika Srpska has been informed of successful combat operations around Srebrenica by the units of the Drina Corps and that they have achieved results which enable them to occupy the very town of Srebrenica." The second paragraph: "The president of the republic is satisfied with the result of combat operations around Srebrenica and has agreed to continue operations in order to take over Srebrenica, disarm Muslim terrorist gangs, and completely demilitarise the Srebrenica enclave." The third paragraph: "The President of Republika Srpska ordered that in the follow-up combat operations, full protection of UNPROFOR members be ensured as well as the Muslim population, and that they be guaranteed safety in the event they cross over into the territory of Republika Srpska." In the last paragraph, it says: "In accordance with the order of the President of Republika Srpska, issue an order to all combat units participating in combat operations around Srebrenica to offer maximum protection and safety to all UNPROFOR members and civilian Muslim population. Order the subordinate units to refrain from destroying civilian targets unless forced to do so due to strong enemy resistance. Ban the torching of residential buildings, and treat civilians and war prisoners in accordance with the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949. "Assistant commander, Major General Zdravko Tolimir." Based on this, I would like to ask you the following: Were you informed by the corps command that there was a change of this kind on the 10th of July and this is why you conducted regrouping and adjustment of forces that you described in your diary on page 0648-6783? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. On the following day, when -- just a moment, please. I need to find my diary so that I can see what I wrote down. On the 10th of July, on page 6 of my Srebrenica diary: "There is a decision to change the axis of the attack of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, (specified in an order.) The forces are being regrouped and are acting in coordination with the Zvornik Brigade as the left flank neighbour to continue the attack in Orahovica, Vogan, Zivkovo Brdo, Kusevice [phoen] village, Bojna, Rajne village, Srebrenica." So based on the information that reached the IKM of the Drina Corps, perhaps it would be relevant to see when that information arrived, at what time it arrived to the IKM. Perhaps you could lower the document a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we go back to this document, if I could, just for the sake of the record, ask that the witness confirm what he is reading from because he said he's going to read from his diary and he's reading from it and I think it would be helpful to have a reference to the ERN number for the record so that we can go back. And I would just ask if the witness could read the eight-digit ERN number on the page he was reading from just so that we have that handy for us in the future. Again, that's from P1444, the witness's diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed that would be very helpful if you could indicate the ERN number and the page number. And I would like to add, are you reading from your original diary or from the copy we all have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I have to give you the page number as denoted by the OTP, then I'm going to be reading from that page, from the photocopy which is identical to the original that is before me. And the number is 0648-6784, and the page number in my diary, marked in red ink, is 6. The date on that page is 10 July 1995, which shows that that was after the document that General Document [as interpreted] had sent to Generals Gvero and Krstic for their information. In my diary on that date, I noted this, the decision to change the direction of attack of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, as specified in the order, and to regroup forces in coordinated action with the 1st Zvornik Brigade as the left neighbour - that's my unit - and continued the attack along the axis of Orahovica, that's the general area, whereas the narrow area is Vogan, Zivkovo Brdo, Pusmulici village, Rajna village, Bojna, the repeater Bojna, and finally in the direction of Srebrenica. And my remark here is that a lot of time was spent in grouping forces from the direction of Alibegovac, Lipovac, Siljato Brdo, Vijogor village, to the newly defined axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Witness. I apologise for not having given you the ERN number immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: My question now is this: In keeping with this particular order about the protection of UNPROFOR forces and the civilian population, did you receive from your corps command any orders about the protection of UNPROFOR forces and the civilian population? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, such tasks had been set out at the beginning of the initial order. In this particular case I did not deem it necessary to record such instances every time I came in contact with my superior officer.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please state clearly, and do it for the record, and can you tell us "yes" or "no," did you receive orders from the corps command about the protection of the civilian population and UNPROFOR forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: And now, please, could the Court produce document D69. Thank you. The document was issued by the Drina Corps on the 8th of July, two days before the 10th, which is the date of the witness's entry that he has just read. Could you please look at the penultimate paragraph, where it says: "The Main Staff has ordered you not to attack UNPROFOR but, rather, to prevent any surprises and stop the Muslims in their intention to join up Srebrenica and Zepa." Thank you. My question is this: From the very outset of the operation, you had been instructed that your target was not either UNPROFOR or the civilian population but something else. What was the target of your operation? Can you tell us, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be very specific, because this is what you are asking me to do, probably because of the time. I've already shared with you the target of the operation, the main goal of the operation. I don't think that that should be repeated. We received repeated orders not to target UNPROFOR and to prevent surprises and intentions of the Muslims to join up the two enclaves in question.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Popovic transcript, page 1811, lines 15 through 17, you said about the protected areas, and I quote: "I wouldn't say under protection but under the shield of UNPROFOR units, there were incursions targeted at our units." My question is this: Could it happen, unbeknownst to UNPROFOR, that there were any kind of actions coming from the enclaves targeting the Serbian population and military targets in Republika Srpska? According to what you know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that it was possible. They could engage in incursions, given the fact that the observation posts manned by UNPROFOR were not close to each other and that they did not engage in full observation activity at all times. But I wouldn't say that those incursions were carried out under UNPROFOR protection, but the mere fact that the UNPROFOR forces were deployed in the area was used by the Muslims as a shield. In other words, they used their presence in order to find passage through a valley, along a river, and carry out their incursions.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing in mind that there were constant contacts between UNPROFOR and the two sides, and that the two sides informed UNPROFOR about their respective activities, let's not waste any more time on -- time on that. Even General Mladic wrote to the command of UNPROFOR in Sarajevo which was at his level. He informed them about the events in February. Already in February he stated that he couldn't consider Srebrenica and Zepa demilitarised zones given the activities that were taking place there. In view of the information that was received, was it possible that there was no knowledge about activities going on in the enclaves and coming out of them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a more specific question. I don't think it was possible for UNPROFOR not to be aware of those activities. What I said in my previous answer was that they could carry out incursions, that they could pass through some areas unobserved, but still UNPROFOR was there to establish the consequences of such incursions. Those incursions could not go unobserved by UNPROFOR in that respect, as it were.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's not show the document, let's just say that in your testimony earlier today you said that no heavy weaponry had been handed over to the Army of Republika Srpska, or at least that you don't know anything about that. And finally, you said in your statement that fire was opened on you from heavy weaponry, weaponry over 12 millimetre in calibre. You said that in the Popovic case on page 11913, when you spoke about the spring offensive -- I apologise. I gave the wrong number. When you entered Srebrenica, fire was opened on you, as you stated, and that fire came from heavy mortars. Can you tell us something about that? Or, rather, from heavy machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you must give us the correct page number of the Popovic case, which is P1197.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Page number is 11887.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 11883 is the correct page number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have the third version. I hope this is the correct one. The question of Mr. Tolimir was: Can you tell us something about that, or, rather, from heavy machine-guns? Do you recall the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the Popovic case testimony -- could you please jog my memory? Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me remind you, the transcript number, page number is 11883. You said that your group, on the 10th of July, was exposed to fire from anti-aircraft weaponry. What kind of weaponry was that and where were they located? The page number is 11883. Thank you. The lines are 5 through 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We have a technical problem again. Now we see it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I adhere by what I stated. Fire was indeed opened from big calibre weaponry, I suppose from anti-aircraft cannons. They were either single-barrelled cannons or even bigger weaponry, and that was after the regrouping of our forces in the Zivkovo Brdo sector. And after we had passed through the Slapovici sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Court please produce P01224. Thank you. This is another document drafted by the BiH army, issued by the command of the 2nd Tuzla Corps. Or, rather, it was sent to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla and it was signed by Ramiz Becirevic, who was Naser Oric's deputy in Srebrenica. He sent it to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. We are interested in the second page of this document. And since you are an artillery man, could you please explain something that we see on the second page. It says, "Artillery units of anti-aircraft defence." This is a big title in capital letters. And then under number 1, or rather from 1 through 25 on this page, you see a list of departments and tools and pieces which are used by the unit. Ramiz reports on what he has and what he has assigned to the task. He reports back to his corps. Could you please explain to us, as an artillery man, can you explain for the Trial Chamber what is PAT 20/21 and all the other designations of heavy artillery? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that this was under seal in the Popovic case. Is that correct, Mr. Thayer? In that case, it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You're correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: My question for the witness is this: I didn't know that the document was under seal. My question is this: Does this testify to the fact that there was heavy weaponry in Srebrenica and that there were departments or troops assigned to those pieces? Were you aware of the existence of a 20-millimetre anti-aircraft cannon?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It arises from this that there were crews or departments, that there was a 20-millimetre cannon, which required a crew of over three men at a time. There were several squadrons and the 28th Division had 20-millimetre uni-barrelled cannons as well as anti-aircraft machine-guns on their strength. The latter is a smaller calibre type of weaponry where the 20-millimetre cannons are considered heavy weaponry. And all that was used in the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina to open fire on infantry troops.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTION AT THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you become exposed to fire from such weaponry from PAMs or from cannons? Because here, item number 8 shows a 20-millimetre PAM.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fire was opened from both, as well as from infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we are at the end of today's hearing. You have to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just tender this document into evidence? And we will continue tomorrow, I suppose. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This -- we will deal with that tomorrow because I see a problem. These are all P documents, MFI'd from the list of the Prosecution but not used with this witness through examination-in-chief and I have to clarify with the Registry if it will be appropriate to have this as a P number while you are using that during the cross-examination in fact as a D document, but I think we should check that until tomorrow. Thank you. We have to adjourn for the day. May I remind you that you're not allowed to have contact with any of the parties during the break. We are resuming tomorrow in the afternoon unless you get an information that we will sit in the morning, but that will be -- this information will be, at the earliest possible, in the late afternoon. It depends on the progress of the other trial. We adjourn.
